reconcile.note: Jamieson, Fausset & Brown reconcile the totals by reading Paul's 23,000 as those killed by the plague alone, while Moses' 24,000 adds those the judges executed.

discrepancy.note: Isaac of Troki calls Paul's twenty-three thousand a plain error against Moses' twenty-four thousand for the same plague.

quotes.text: In this brief passage there is an error, which in every other work might pass unnoticed. A book, which assumes to be dictated by inspiration, ought to be accurate in every particular. In Numbers xxv., we read ihai four and twenty thousand and not three and twenty thousand^ fell by the visitation of pestilence.
quotes.attr: Isaac ben Abraham Troki (d. 1594), Faith Strengthened (Chizzuk Emunah), trans. Moses Mocatta (1851), ch. LXXXVI, on Numbers 25:9 and 1 Corinthians 10:8.

sides.snippet: Those who died by the plague were twenty-four thousand.
sides.verseText: Those who died by the plague were twenty-four thousand.

sides.snippet: in one day twenty-three thousand fell
sides.verseText: Neither let us commit sexual immorality, as some of them committed, and in one day twenty-three thousand fell.
